channel.title: Nick Cerbone Diary
channel.description: Personal diary and blog posts by Nick Cerbone.

item.title: The Question We Leave Our Children
item.description: Machine personhood is not our question to settle. It is the one we hand down — sharpened, or dull.

item.title: After Scarcity
item.description: When intelligence gets cheap, value migrates to land, time, attention, trust, and care.

item.title: The Long Life We Are Not Ready For
item.description: A 50-year-old does the math on partial reprogramming, second lifetimes, and readiness.

item.title: The Machine at the Kitchen Table
item.description: Renting intelligence by the month, or owning it in the house — subsidiarity at household scale.

item.title: Product Liability, Not Malpractice
item.description: A machine a thousand times better than the best surgeon will still fail one day. Who answers for it?

item.title: When Answers Are Free
item.description: Schools were built to ration scarce information. The scarcity ended. The formation remains.

item.title: You Cannot Own Knowledge
item.description: Property is for rival goods. Knowledge is not one, and AI is finishing the argument.

item.title: The Assembly Line Comes for Knowledge Work
item.description: Knowledge workers are meeting the artisans' moment — and abundance has two sides.

item.title: Caesar and the Machine
item.description: A Catholic response to Pope Leo XIV's encyclical Magnifica Humanitas on AI governance, subsidiarity, and digital empire.

item.title: He Has Gone Before Us: Reflections for the Solemnity of the Ascension
item.description: A reflection for Ascension Sunday, May 17, 2026.

item.title: A Miracle of Faith: Sts. Nereus and Achilleus
item.description: A reflection for their feast day, May 12.

item.title: Notes on an Incident
item.description: Instructure calls it an incident. The students are calling it finals week.

item.title: Public Data Is Not Public
item.description: Public information is often legally available and practically unreachable.
